> sp + opts(axis.text.x=theme_blank()) + facet_grid(.~variable)+ylim(0,25)
>
> And I get this graph:
>
>
>
> I prefer the layout of first graph, but it irritates me that I have "double" values of each observation. How do I avoid this?
>
> Thanks!

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Facets and qplot and/or ggplot
parts: If you set your alpha to 0.50 and you're seeing two colors (one darker than the other) then it's because you have points that are being plotted on top of each other. The way around this is to make the graph huge so jitter has plenty of room to separate the points or make your points very small. I wonder if perhaps you'd be better off with a summary of your data rather than plotting every point. Perhaps a boxplot?

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Facets and qplot and/or ggplot
parts:
Ah, OK, so you have an overplotting problem. If alpha<1 there aren't
two different colors, but obviously when dots overlap the alphas are
additive (indeed, this is the whole point). Other ways to deal with
this include axis transforms, geom_histogram, geom_density2d, and as
Brandon suggested, summarizing your data before plotting.

Ben
